mainTopic: The יסוד requirement and placements of blood, and the source for how long a בכור may be eaten, including the debate in יבנה over היקש
overview: Earlier on this daf, the גמרא learned that בכור, מעשר and פסח need their blood placed where the altar has a יסוד, by comparing them to the עולה. Now it brings a פסוק showing that the עולה itself needs the יסוד. It explains why these offerings do not also copy the עולה's 'two placements that are four': 'around' is written for עולה, חטאת and אשם, and verses that repeat the same rule do not teach other cases. Next the גמרא turns to the משנה's line about the בכור and brings a ברייתא: the פסוק compares the בכור to the חזה ושוק of שלמים, so it is eaten for two days and one night. The ברייתא then tells of a debate in יבנה. רבי טרפון and the young רבי יוסי הגלילי trade logical comparisons, until רבי עקיבא settles it with the היקש from the פסוק and the extra words 'לך יהיה'. רבי ישמעאל says רבי עקיבא should not have conceded the comparison to a תודה, because something learned by a היקש cannot teach by a היקש. The גמרא explains how each תנא uses 'לך יהיה' and 'בשרם', including the law that a blemished בכור goes to the כהן. Finally, it shows that their real argument is whether a law from a היקש plus another source counts as a היקש. It then tests both views against the יום כפור sprinklings.

steps.title: Where do we learn that a burnt offering itself needs the base?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that the blood of a עולה must be placed on a part of the altar that has a יסוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the burnt offering itself, where do we learn this from?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא learned that other offerings need the יסוד because they are compared to the עולה. Now it asks where we know that the עולה itself needs the יסוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A comparison only works if the original rule has a firm source. Since the rule for בכור, מעשר and פסח depends on the עולה, the גמרא must show where the עולה gets this rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Burnt offering, burned completely on the altar
Itself
From where do we know this?

phrases.english: And the burnt offering itself, from where do we know it?
phrases.notes: He means: where do we know that the עולה's blood must go on a part of the altar that has a base.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעוֹלָה גּוּפַהּ מְנָלַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the source of the rule that the earlier comparison was built on.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source that a עולה requires יסוד.

steps.title: The verse 'the base of the altar of the burnt offering'
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק links the יסוד to 'the altar of the burnt offering,' which teaches that an obligatory עולה needs the יסוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'At the base of the altar of the burnt offering.' This teaches that an obligatory burnt offering needs the base.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a פסוק that calls the altar 'the altar of the burnt offering' together with its base. This shows that the עולה's blood belongs where there is a יסוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק is talking about the blood of a חטאת bull, so there was no need to mention the עולה. The extra mention connects the יסוד to the עולה, and the גמרא reads it as a rule for עולת חובה.

keyTerms.meaning: The base, the bottom step that runs along the altar
A burnt offering brought as an obligation
Requires

phrases.english: As it is written: 'At the base of the altar of the burnt offering'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 4:7

phrases.aramaic: לִמֵּד עַל עוֹלַת חוֹבָה שֶׁטְּעוּנָה יְסוֹד.
phrases.english: It teaches about an obligatory burnt offering that it requires the base.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּכְתִיב: ״אֶל יְסוֹד מִזְבַּח הָעוֹלָה״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 1.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק 'אל יסוד מזבח העולה' teaches that an obligatory עולה requires the יסוד.

steps.title: Then they should also need two placements that are four
steps.stepSummary: If בכור, מעשר and פסח learn from the עולה, maybe they should also copy the עולה's 'two placements that are four.'
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, just as there it is two placements that are four, so too here it should be two placements that are four!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the comparison. If we learn the יסוד from the עולה, why not learn all of the עולה's blood rules, including its 'two placements that are four'?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A comparison usually carries over the whole rule. The עולה gets two placements on opposite corners, which reach all four sides. But the משנה says בכור, מעשר and פסח need only one placement, so the comparison seems to prove too much.

keyTerms.meaning: Just as there (in the source case)
So too here (in the learned case)
Two placements of blood on opposite corners that cover all four sides of the altar

steps.confusionAlert: 'Here' does not mean the עולה. It means בכור, מעשר and פסח, which learned the יסוד from the עולה earlier on the daf.

phrases.english: If so, just as there
phrases.notes: 'There' is the עולה, the case we learn from.

phrases.english: it is two placements that are four,

phrases.english: so too here, two placements that are four?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי – מָה לְהַלָּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the comparison to the עולה by saying it would carry over too much.
steps.kashyaTarget: The comparison from עולה to בכור, מעשר and פסח.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A comparison should carry over the full blood rule, so these offerings should need two placements that are four, against the משנה's single placement.

steps.title: אביי: two verses that say the same thing do not teach
steps.stepSummary: אביי says 'around' is written for both עולה and חטאת, so these are שני כתובין הבאין כאחד, and they cannot teach other cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Why do I need the Torah to write 'around' for the burnt offering and 'around' for the sin offering? They are two verses that come as one, and any two verses that come as one do not teach.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers that the 'all four sides' rule cannot spread to other offerings. The Torah wrote it twice, for עולה and for חטאת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the rule applied to every offering, writing it once would have been enough. Writing it twice for two offerings shows it belongs only to them. That is the rule of שני כתובין הבאין כאחד אין מלמדין, so the comparison carries over the יסוד but not the four sides.

keyTerms.meaning: Around, meaning the blood reaches all four sides
Sin offering
Two verses that teach the same rule
They do not teach (the rule to other cases)

steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why בכור, מעשר and פסח need the יסוד like an עולה but only one placement of blood.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
Why do I need it to write 'around' for the burnt offering,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 1:5

phrases.english: and 'around' for the sin offering?
phrases.notes: ויקרא 8:15

phrases.english: They are two verses that come as one,

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: לְמָה לִי לְמִכְתַּב ״סָבִיב״ בְּעוֹלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the comparison with the rule of שני כתובין הבאין כאחד אין מלמדין.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The comparison to the עולה would carry over the two placements that are four.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Around' is written for both עולה and חטאת, so it does not spread to other offerings. Only the יסוד carries over.

steps.title: What about the opinion that two such verses do teach?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says אביי's answer only works for the view that two verses do not teach. What about the view that they do?
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well for the one who says they do not teach. But for the one who says they do teach, what is there to say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that אביי's answer depends on an argument. Some hold that two verses saying the same thing do teach other cases, and for them the challenge comes back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the opinion that two verses do teach, 'around' in עולה and חטאת would spread to all offerings. Then בכור, מעשר and פסח should need all four sides again.

keyTerms.meaning: This works out well
According to the one who says
What is there to say?

phrases.english: This works well according to the one who says they do not teach,
but according to the one who says they do teach,
what is there to say?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנִיחָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר אֵין מְלַמְּדִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges אביי's answer by pointing to the other opinion.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's answer based on שני כתובין הבאין כאחד אין מלמדין.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: For the view that two such verses do teach, the 'around' rule would spread to all offerings, and the challenge of step 3 returns.

steps.title: With the guilt offering there are three verses, and three certainly do not teach
steps.stepSummary: 'Around' is also written for the אשם, so there are three verses, and everyone agrees three verses do not teach.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is three, with the guilt offering, and three certainly do not teach.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the 'around' rule appears three times: עולה, חטאת and אשם. Everyone agrees that three verses saying the same thing do not teach other cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even the opinion that two verses teach agrees that three do not, because writing it a third time clearly shows it is limited. So both opinions agree that בכור, מעשר and פסח need only one placement.

keyTerms.meaning: Guilt offering
Certainly

steps.whatToRemember: בכור, מעשר and פסח learn the יסוד from the עולה, but not its two placements that are four. 'Around' is written for עולה, חטאת and אשם, and three verses that say the same thing certainly do not teach.

phrases.english: With the guilt offering, there are three,
phrases.notes: The אשם also has 'around' written about it, in ויקרא 7:2.

phrases.english: and three certainly do not teach.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 5 so that both opinions reach the same result.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Adds a third verse, so the answer works according to every opinion.

steps.terutzMaskana: With the אשם there are three verses, and three verses certainly do not teach, so the four sides do not spread.

steps.title: Where do we learn the eating time of a בכור?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's line about the בכור. It brings a ברייתא that asks for the source that a בכור is eaten for two days and one night.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: the firstborn is eaten by the priests. The Rabbis taught: from where do we know that a firstborn is eaten for two days and a night?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting the משנה about the בכור. A ברייתא asks for the source of its eating time, which sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier steps dealt with where the blood is placed on the מזבח. Now the focus moves to how long the meat may be eaten. The ברייתא takes the rule of two days and one night as given and asks only where it comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: Firstborn male animal, brought as a קרבן and eaten by the כהנים
From where do we know?
For two days and the one night between them

phrases.english: The firstborn is eaten by the priests.
The Rabbis taught:
From where do we know about the firstborn
that it is eaten for two days and a night?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִנַּיִן לַבְּכוֹר שֶׁנֶּאֱכָל לִשְׁנֵי יָמִים וְלַיְלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה, moving from blood placement to eating time.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source for the בכור being eaten for two days and one night.

steps.title: The פסוק compares בכור to the breast and thigh of שלמים
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says the בכור's meat is 'like the breast of waving and the right thigh.' That links it to שלמים, so it is eaten for two days and one night like them.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: 'And their meat shall be yours, like the breast of waving and like the right thigh.' The verse compared the firstborn to the breast and thigh of peace offerings. Just as peace offerings are eaten for two days and one night, so too the firstborn is eaten for two days and one night.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its own question with a פסוק that puts the בכור side by side with the שלמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חזה ושוק are the parts of the שלמים given to the כהן. Because the תורה describes the בכור's meat 'like' those parts, it makes a היקש, a comparison made by the פסוק itself. So the בכור takes on the שלמים' eating time of two days and one night.

keyTerms.meaning: A comparison made by the פסוק itself, placing two things side by side
Breast and thigh, the parts of the שלמים given to the כהן
Peace offerings, eaten for two days and one night
Waving, the ceremony done with the breast

steps.whatToRemember: The source for the בכור's two days and one night is a היקש to the חזה ושוק of שלמים.

phrases.english: As it says:
"And their meat shall be yours
phrases.notes: במדבר 18:18

phrases.english: like the breast of waving and like the right thigh"
The verse compared it

steps.triggerLanguage: הִקִּישׁוֹ הַכָּתוּב לְחָזֶה וָשׁוֹק שֶׁל שְׁלָמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question asked in step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A היקש in במדבר 18:18 links the בכור to the חזה ושוק of שלמים, giving it two days and one night.

steps.title: In יבנה, רבי טרפון rules two days and one night
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא tells a story. The Sages in יבנה asked how long a בכור is eaten, and רבי טרפון answered two days and one night.
steps.simpleTranslation: This question was asked before the Sages in the vineyard in יבנה: for how long is a firstborn eaten? רבי טרפון answered and said: for two days and one night.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא begins a story about this same question. רבי טרפון gives the ruling, which sets up a debate about his source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling matches what the ברייתא just learned from the פסוק. The story is not about a new ruling. It is about how one proves it, as the next steps show.

keyTerms.meaning: The 'vineyard' in יבנה, the Sages' study hall
Answered and said

phrases.english: And this question was asked
before the Sages in the vineyard in Yavne:
phrases.notes: The 'vineyard' here means the place where the Sages learned together in יבנה.

phrases.english: For how long is a firstborn eaten?
Rabbi Tarfon answered and said:
For two days and one night.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְזוֹ שְׁאֵלָה נִשְׁאֲלָה לִפְנֵי חֲכָמִים בַּכֶּרֶם בְּיַבְנֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same ruling, now presented through a story in the study hall.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי טרפון: a בכור is eaten for two days and one night.

steps.title: A new student, רבי יוסי הגלילי, asks for the source
steps.stepSummary: A student in his first visit to the study hall, רבי יוסי הגלילי, asks רבי טרפון where he learns this.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was one student there who came to the study hall before the Sages for the first time, and his name was רבי יוסי הגלילי. He said to him: My teacher, where do you get this from?
steps.whatsHappening: A brand-new student asks רבי טרפון for his source. This sets up רבי טרפון's proof in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is not an attack yet. It is a request for the reasoning behind the ruling, which opens the door to the debate.

keyTerms.meaning: For the first time
Where do you get this from?

phrases.english: There was one student there
who came to the study hall
before the Sages for the first time,
and his name was Rabbi Yosei HaGelili.
He said to him: My teacher, where do you get this from?

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי, מִנַּיִן לָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the ruling given in step 9.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: רבי טרפון's source for two days and one night.

steps.title: רבי טרפון: בכור is like שלמים, both קדשים קלים
steps.stepSummary: רבי טרפון says that שלמים and בכור are both קדשים קלים, so the בכור is eaten for two days and one night like שלמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: My son, peace offerings are offerings of lesser holiness, and a firstborn is an offering of lesser holiness. Just as peace offerings are eaten for two days and one night, so too a firstborn is eaten for two days and one night.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי טרפון answers by comparing the בכור to the שלמים because both belong to the same holiness level.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike the ברייתא in step 8, רבי טרפון does not quote the פסוק here. He uses a logical comparison: things in the same category, קדשים קלים, should share an eating time. A logical comparison like this can be answered with a different comparison, which is what happens next.

keyTerms.meaning: Offerings of lesser holiness, like שלמים and בכור
My son, a warm way a teacher addresses a student
Just as ... so too (the form of a comparison)

phrases.english: He said to him: My son,
peace offerings are offerings of lesser holiness,
and a firstborn is an offering of lesser holiness;
just as peace offerings are eaten
for two days and one night,
so too a firstborn is eaten
for two days and one night.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up this proof with the ברייתא's proof in step 8. There it was a היקש from a פסוק. Here רבי טרפון uses a comparison based on both being קדשים קלים.
steps.triggerLanguage: בְּנִי, שְׁלָמִים קָדָשִׁים קַלִּים, וּבְכוֹר קָדָשִׁים קַלִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי יוסי הגלילי's request for a source.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Both שלמים and בכור are קדשים קלים, so the בכור shares the שלמים' eating time.

steps.title: רבי יוסי הגלילי: maybe בכור is like חטאת and אשם
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי הגלילי offers a competing comparison. A בכור is a gift to the כהן like חטאת and אשם, so maybe it should be eaten for only one day and one night.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: My teacher, a firstborn is a gift to the priest, and a sin offering and guilt offering are a gift to the priest. Just as a sin offering and guilt offering are eaten for a day and a night, so too a firstborn should be eaten for a day and a night!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי הגלילי challenges רבי טרפון's comparison by offering a different one that gives a shorter eating time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי טרפון compared based on holiness level. רבי יוסי הגלילי compares based on who gets the meat: the בכור goes to the כהן, just like חטאת and אשם. Since both comparisons seem to work, רבי טרפון's logic alone cannot decide the question.

keyTerms.meaning: A gift given to the כהן
Sin offering and guilt offering, eaten by כהנים for one day and one night
For one day and the following night

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the weakness of a comparison built only on logic: someone can always find another feature that points the other way. That is why the ברייתא's source from a פסוק in step 8 is so important.

phrases.english: He said to him: My teacher,
a firstborn is a gift to the priest,
and a sin offering and guilt offering are a gift to the priest;
just as a sin offering and guilt offering are for a day and a night,
so too a firstborn should be for a day and a night!

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי, בְּכוֹר מַתָּנָה לַכֹּהֵן, וְחַטָּאת וְאָשָׁם מַתָּנָה לַכֹּהֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי טרפון's comparison from step 11 with a competing comparison.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי טרפון's comparison of בכור to שלמים because both are קדשים קלים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A different shared feature, being a gift to the כהן, links בכור to חטאת and אשם. That would give a shorter time of one day and one night, so the first comparison is not decisive.

steps.title: רבי טרפון adds that neither שלמים nor בכור comes for a sin
steps.stepSummary: רבי טרפון defends his comparison. A בכור is closer to שלמים because neither one comes to atone for a sin, so the בכור shares the two-day eating time of שלמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Let us judge one thing from the thing it is most like, and learn one thing from another. Just as שלמים do not come to atone for a sin, a בכור also does not come for a sin. And just as שלמים are eaten for two days and one night, a בכור is also eaten for two days and one night.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי טרפון answers רבי יוסי הגלילי's challenge. He shows that the בכור matches שלמים in another way, not just in being קדשים קלים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי הגלילי had said the בכור is like חטאת and אשם because all three are gifts to the כהן. רבי טרפון points to another shared trait: חטאת and אשם come because of a sin, but שלמים and בכור do not. Since the בכור is most like שלמים, it should copy their eating time.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us judge one thing from another, meaning we compare a case to the one it most resembles
and let us learn (copy the other laws over)
comes to atone for a sin
one night

phrases.aramaic: מָה שְׁלָמִים נֶאֱכָלִים לִשְׁנֵי יָמִים וְלַיְלָה אֶחָד –
phrases.english: Just as peace offerings are eaten for two days and one night,

phrases.aramaic: אַף בְּכוֹר נֶאֱכָל לִשְׁנֵי יָמִים וְלַיְלָה אֶחָד.
phrases.english: so too a firstborn is eaten for two days and one night.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ: נָדוּן דָּבָר מִתּוֹךְ דָּבָר, וְנִלְמַד דָּבָר מִתּוֹךְ דָּבָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends רבי טרפון's comparison against רבי יוסי הגלילי's competing comparison in step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Strengthens the original comparison with an additional shared trait (not brought for a sin).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Being a gift to the כהן makes the בכור like חטאת and אשם, so it would be eaten for one day.
steps.terutzMaskana: Not being brought for a sin makes the בכור like שלמים, so it is eaten for two days and one night.

steps.title: רבי יוסי הגלילי adds that neither חטאת, אשם nor בכור comes as a vow or gift
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי הגלילי uses the same method against רבי טרפון. חטאת, אשם and בכור are all gifts to the כהן, and none of them can be brought by choice as a נדר or נדבה, so the בכור should be eaten for one day like them.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: My teacher, let us judge one thing from another, and learn one thing from another. חטאת and אשם are a gift to the כהן, and a בכור is a gift to the כהן. Just as חטאת and אשם are not brought as a נדר or a נדבה, a בכור is also not brought as a נדר or a נדבה. And just as חטאת and אשם are eaten for one day, a בכור is also eaten for one day!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי הגלילי turns רבי טרפון's own method around. He finds an extra trait that the בכור shares with חטאת and אשם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי טרפון found one extra link to שלמים: not coming for a sin. רבי יוסי הגלילי answers with an extra link to חטאת and אשם: none of them can be brought by choice. Now each side has an equally strong comparison, so the logic alone cannot decide the question.

keyTerms.meaning: a gift to the כהן (the כהן gets the meat)
a vow, where a person says 'I take upon myself to bring an offering'
a free-will gift, where a person says 'this animal is an offering'
sin offering and guilt offering

steps.confusionAlert: 'Eaten for one day' here means one day together with the night that follows it. It does not mean only daytime hours.

phrases.english: He said to him: My teacher,

phrases.aramaic: נָדוּן דָּבָר מִדָּבָר, יִלְמַד דָּבָר מִדָּבָר;
phrases.english: let us judge a matter from a matter, and learn a matter from a matter;
phrases.notes: He is using רבי טרפון's own words to argue for the other side.

phrases.english: a sin offering and a guilt offering are a gift to the priest,
and a firstborn is a gift to the priest.

phrases.aramaic: מָה חַטָּאת וְאָשָׁם אֵין בָּאִין בְּנֶדֶר וּנְדָבָה –
phrases.english: Just as a sin offering and a guilt offering do not come as a vow or a gift offering,
so too a firstborn does not come as a vow or a gift offering.

phrases.aramaic: מָה חַטָּאת וְאָשָׁם נֶאֱכָלִין לְיוֹם אֶחָד –
phrases.english: Just as a sin offering and a guilt offering are eaten for one day,
so too a firstborn should be eaten for one day!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ: רַבִּי, נָדוּן דָּבָר מִדָּבָר, יִלְמַד דָּבָר מִדָּבָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Counters רבי טרפון's added trait in step 13 with an equally strong added trait for the opposite comparison.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי טרפון's reasoning that the בכור matches שלמים because neither comes for a sin.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The בכור shares two traits with חטאת and אשם (gift to the כהן, not brought by choice). That comparison is just as strong, so the בכור could be eaten for one day.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא brings a הקש from the פסוק to the breast and thigh of שלמים
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא jumps in, and רבי טרפון withdraws. He shows that the פסוק itself compares the בכור's meat to the breast and thigh of שלמים, so the בכור is eaten for two days and one night.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא jumped in, and רבי טרפון stepped back. He said to him: The פסוק says, 'And their meat shall be yours,' and the פסוק compares them to the breast and thigh of שלמים. Just as שלמים are eaten for two days and one night, a בכור is also eaten for two days and one night.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא jumps in and takes over the argument, and רבי טרפון steps back. He stops arguing from logic and brings proof from the פסוק instead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The logical comparisons were stuck, because each side had an equal match. רבי עקיבא uses a הקש, a comparison the Torah itself makes, which is stronger than our own reasoning. The פסוק puts the בכור's meat next to the breast and thigh of שלמים, so it gets the שלמים eating time.

keyTerms.meaning: jumped in
stepped back, withdrew from the discussion
the פסוק compared them (a הֶקֵּשׁ, a comparison made by the Torah itself)
the breast and the thigh, the parts of a שלמים given to the כהן

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the same source the ברייתא gave in step 8. Now we see that it comes from רבי עקיבא, and that it is needed because the logical comparisons could not settle the question.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva jumped in,
and Rabbi Tarfon withdrew.
He said to him: But the verse says:
phrases.notes: רבי עקיבא is now speaking to רבי יוסי הגלילי.

phrases.english: "And their flesh shall be yours"
phrases.notes: במדבר 18:18

phrases.aramaic: הִקִּישָׁן הַכָּתוּב לְחָזֶה וָשׁוֹק שֶׁל שְׁלָמִים;
phrases.english: the verse compares them to the breast and thigh of peace offerings.

phrases.aramaic: מָה שְׁלָמִים נֶאֱכָלִין לִשְׁנֵי יָמִים וְלַיְלָה אֶחָד,
phrases.english: Just as peace offerings are eaten for two days and one night,

phrases.aramaic: אַף בְּכוֹר נֶאֱכָל לִשְׁנֵי יָמִים וְלַיְלָה אֶחָד.
phrases.english: so too a firstborn is eaten for two days and one night.

steps.triggerLanguage: קָפַץ רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא, וְנִסְתַּלֵּק רַבִּי טַרְפוֹן. אָמַר לוֹ: הֲרֵי הוּא אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the stuck logical comparisons and answers step 14 with a comparison taken from the פסוק itself.
steps.raayaObject: That a בכור is eaten for two days and one night.
steps.raayaSupportSource: במדבר 18:18, 'And their flesh shall be yours, like the breast of waving and the right thigh', which compares the בכור to the breast and thigh of שלמים.

steps.title: רבי יוסי הגלילי says the comparison could be to the breast and thigh of a תודה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי הגלילי pushes back. The פסוק only says 'breast and thigh', and a תודה also has a breast and thigh. So he compares the בכור to a תודה, which is eaten for only one day and one night.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: You compared it to the breast and thigh of שלמים, but I compare it to the breast and thigh of a תודה. Just as a תודה is eaten for a day and a night, a בכור is also eaten for a day and a night!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי הגלילי accepts that the פסוק makes a comparison. He argues that it does not tell us which offering's breast and thigh it means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא assumed the breast and thigh in the פסוק belong to regular שלמים. A תודה also has a breast and thigh, so the פסוק could fit it just as well. If so, the בכור gets the shorter time of a תודה: one day and one night.

keyTerms.meaning: thanksgiving offering, eaten for only one day and one night
you compared it
I compare it
for a day and a night

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ: הִיקַּשְׁתּוֹ לְחָזֶה וָשׁוֹק שֶׁל שְׁלָמִים,
phrases.english: He said to him: You compared it to the breast and thigh of peace offerings,

phrases.aramaic: וַאֲנִי מַקִּישׁוֹ לְחָזֶה וָשׁוֹק שֶׁל תּוֹדָה –
phrases.english: but I compare it to the breast and thigh of a thanks offering.
Just as a thanks offering is eaten for a day and a night,
so too a firstborn should be eaten for a day and a night!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ: הִיקַּשְׁתּוֹ לְחָזֶה וָשׁוֹק שֶׁל שְׁלָמִים, וַאֲנִי מַקִּישׁוֹ לְחָזֶה וָשׁוֹק שֶׁל תּוֹדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי עקיבא's הקש by showing that the same פסוק can be read as a comparison to a תודה.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רבי עקיבא's conclusion that the הקש points to two days and one night. He does not reject the existence of the הקש.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The פסוק does not name which offering's breast and thigh it means. A תודה also has a breast and thigh, and it is eaten for only one day and one night.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא Finds a Second Day in the Extra Words
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא answers רבי יוסי הגלילי. Even if the בכור were compared to a תודה, the extra words 'לך יהיה' add another day of eating to the בכור.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא said to him: The פסוק says, 'And their flesh shall be yours.' The פסוק did not need to say 'it shall be yours' a second time. So why does it say 'it shall be yours'? The פסוק is adding another day of eating to the בכור.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא answers רבי יוסי הגלילי's comparison to a תודה with a new proof. He points to extra words in the same פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי הגלילי said the 'breast and thigh' comparison could just as well point to a תודה, which is eaten for only one day. רבי עקיבא does not fight that point. Instead he notes that 'לך יהיה' is said twice, and he reads the extra phrase as adding a second day for the בכור.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'the teaching says'; here it asks why the פסוק needed these words
Another 'being', meaning one more day on which the meat may be eaten
'And their flesh shall be yours' (במדבר 18:18), the פסוק about the בכור

phrases.english: He (Rabbi Akiva) said to him: But it says:
'And their flesh shall be yours'
phrases.notes: במדבר 18:18. The same פסוק ends with 'it shall be yours' a second time.

phrases.english: since there was no need for the verse to say 'it shall be yours'
so why does the verse say 'it shall be yours'?
The verse added another day of eating for the firstborn.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ: הֲרֵי הוּא אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the דחיה in step 16, which compared the בכור to a תודה
steps.terutzResolutionType: New proof from a repeated phrase in the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Comparing the בכור to a תודה would limit it to one day
steps.terutzMaskana: The extra 'לך יהיה' adds a second day, so the בכור is eaten for two days and one night

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל Says the Thanks-Offering Comparison Fails
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל says רבי עקיבא should not have given in. A תודה only gets its breast-and-thigh law through a היקש from שלמים, and something learned through a היקש cannot teach again through a היקש. So the first proof, from שלמים, was correct all along.
steps.simpleTranslation: When these words were said before רבי ישמעאל, he said to them: Go out and tell רבי עקיבא, 'You made a mistake.' Where does a תודה get its breast-and-thigh law from? From שלמים. Can something learned through a היקש turn around and teach through a היקש? So you do not need to argue from the last wording of the פסוק. Argue from the first wording.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ישמעאל hears the debate and knocks down רבי יוסי הגלילי's comparison to a תודה. He also tells רבי עקיבא that his first argument was good enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The breast and thigh of a תודה are never stated outright for the כהן. We know them only by comparing the תודה to שלמים. There is a rule that a law learned through a היקש cannot be passed on through a second היקש, so the בכור cannot be compared to a תודה. The 'breast and thigh' in the פסוק must point straight to שלמים, which gives the בכור two days.

keyTerms.meaning: A comparison the תורה makes by placing two things side by side in a פסוק

keyTerms.term: דָּבָר הַלָּמֵד בְּהֶיקֵּשׁ חוֹזֵר וּמְלַמֵּד בְּהֶיקֵּשׁ
keyTerms.meaning: Can something learned through a היקש go on to teach through a היקש? (The answer here is no)
You made a mistake
The first wording and the last wording of the פסוק

steps.confusionAlert: רבי ישמעאל agrees with רבי עקיבא's result: two days for a בכור. He disagrees only about the proof. רבי עקיבא's first proof, from שלמים, was correct, so he did not need the extra words.

phrases.aramaic: וּכְשֶׁנֶּאְמְרוּ דְּבָרִים לִפְנֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל, אָמַר לָהֶן:
phrases.english: And when these matters were said before Rabbi Yishmael, he said to them:

phrases.aramaic: צְאוּ וְאִמְרוּ לוֹ לְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא: טָעִיתָה.
phrases.english: Go out and tell Rabbi Akiva: You made a mistake.
phrases.notes: His mistake was giving in to רבי יוסי הגלילי's comparison to a תודה.

phrases.english: From where does a thanks offering learn its law? From a peace offering.
[And can] something that is learned through a juxtaposition
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets is part of the corrected wording.

phrases.english: turn around and teach through a juxtaposition?!

phrases.aramaic: הָא אֵין עָלֶיךָ לִידּוֹן בְּלָשׁוֹן אַחֲרוֹן,
phrases.english: So you need not argue from the last wording,
phrases.notes: The 'last wording' is the extra 'לך יהיה'.

phrases.english: but rather from the first wording.
phrases.notes: That is רבי עקיבא's first proof: the 'breast and thigh' comparison to שלמים.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּכְשֶׁנֶּאְמְרוּ דְּבָרִים לִפְנֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the תודה comparison from step 16, which made the proof in step 17 unnecessary
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רבי יוסי הגלילי's comparison of the בכור to a תודה, and so also רבי עקיבא's concession
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A תודה's breast-and-thigh law comes only through a היקש, so it cannot be passed on to a בכור by another היקש

steps.title: What Does רבי ישמעאל Learn From the Extra Words?
steps.stepSummary: Since רבי ישמעאל does not need 'לך יהיה' for the second day, the גמרא asks what he learns from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי ישמעאל, what does he do with this phrase 'it shall be yours'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up the next step with a question. The extra words cannot be wasted, so what are they for according to רבי ישמעאל?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא used 'לך יהיה' to add a day. רבי ישמעאל gets the second day from the שלמים comparison, so the extra words are free. The גמרא wants to know what they teach in his view.

keyTerms.meaning: What does he do with it? (What does he learn from these words?)

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yishmael, this phrase 'it shall be yours'
what does he do with it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל, הַאי ״לְךָ יִהְיֶה״ מַאי עָבֵיד לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from step 18: רבי ישמעאל no longer needs the extra words for the second day
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What רבי ישמעאל learns from the extra phrase 'לך יהיה'

steps.title: A Blemished Firstborn Also Goes to the Priest
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל learns from 'לך יהיה' that a בכור בעל מום (a blemished firstborn) is also a gift to the כהן. Nowhere else does the תורה say this outright.
steps.simpleTranslation: It teaches about a blemished בכור, that it is a gift to the כהן. We do not find this anywhere else in the whole תורה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. For רבי ישמעאל, the extra words teach that even a blemished בכור belongs to the כהן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A blemished בכור cannot be brought as a קרבן, so we might think it is not given to the כהן. The תורה never says outright what to do with it. רבי ישמעאל uses the extra 'לך יהיה' to teach that it still goes to the כהן.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal with a blemish that cannot be brought as a קרבן
A gift given to the כהן

phrases.english: It teaches about a blemished firstborn
that it is a gift to the priest
since we have not found this anywhere in the whole Torah.
phrases.notes: He means nowhere else in the תורה says outright what happens to a blemished בכור.

steps.triggerLanguage: לִימֵּד עַל בְּכוֹר בַּעַל מוּם שֶׁהוּא מַתָּנָה לַכֹּהֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 19
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'לך יהיה' teaches that a בכור בעל מום is also a gift to the כהן

steps.title: רבי עקיבא Learns the Blemished Firstborn From 'Their Flesh'
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא already used 'לך יהיה' for the extra day. He learns that a blemished בכור goes to the כהן from the plural word 'בשרם': one unblemished and one blemished.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי עקיבא learns it from 'their flesh': one is an unblemished בכור and one is a blemished בכור.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains where רבי עקיבא gets the law of a blemished בכור. His extra words are already used up for the second day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'בשרם' means 'their flesh', in the plural. רבי עקיבא reads the plural as two kinds of בכור: a תם (unblemished) and a בעל מום (blemished). Both go to the כהן.

keyTerms.meaning: Unblemished, fit to be brought as a קרבן
He learns (derives) it

phrases.english: And Rabbi Akiva learns it from 'their flesh':
one unblemished and one blemished.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא יָלֵיף לֵיהּ מִ״בְּשָׂרָם״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רבי עקיבא's source for the blemished-בכור law that רבי ישמעאל learned in step 20
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The plural 'בשרם' covers both an unblemished and a blemished בכור

steps.title: How רבי ישמעאל Reads the Plural 'Their Flesh'
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל does not learn the blemished בכור from 'בשרם'. He reads the plural as covering all the kinds of firstborn animals mentioned in the פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי ישמעאל says that 'their flesh' refers to these firstborn animals.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבי ישמעאל does not use 'בשרם' the way רבי עקיבא does. This closes the question of how each one reads the extra words. Next, the גמרא asks what their real disagreement is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plural 'their' is needed for a simple reason in רבי ישמעאל's view. The פסוק lists several kinds of firstborn animals, and 'their flesh' refers to all of them. So the plural teaches nothing about a blemished בכור, and he needs 'לך יהיה' for that.

keyTerms.meaning: Those firstborn animals (the kinds listed in the פסוק)

steps.whatToRemember: Both תנאים agree that a בכור is eaten for two days and one night, and that a blemished בכור goes to the כהן. They differ only on the sources. For רבי עקיבא, 'לך יהיה' adds the second day and 'בשרם' teaches the blemished בכור. For רבי ישמעאל, the שלמים comparison gives the two days and 'לך יהיה' teaches the blemished בכור. רבי ישמעאל holds that a בכור cannot be compared to a תודה, because the תודה's law came through a היקש. Step 24 explains why רבי עקיבא allowed that comparison.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yishmael: from 'their flesh'
he says it means the flesh of these firstborn animals.
phrases.notes: The פסוק before it mentions firstborn cattle, sheep and goats, so 'their' points to all of them.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל, מִ״בְּשָׂרָם״ דְּהָנָךְ בְּכוֹרוֹת קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why רבי ישמעאל does not accept רבי עקיבא's reading of 'בשרם' from step 21
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: For רבי ישמעאל, the plural 'בשרם' refers to the several kinds of firstborn animals in the פסוק

steps.title: What exactly are they arguing about?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the real disagreement is between רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: About what do they disagree?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the two תנאים are really arguing about. This question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides seem to accept that something learned through a היקש cannot teach again through a היקש. So the גמרא wants to find the exact point where they part ways about the תודה and the בכור.

keyTerms.meaning: About what do they disagree?
A comparison the תורה makes by placing two topics side by side

phrases.english: About what do they disagree?
phrases.notes: "They" means רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא, from the earlier steps about the תודה and the בכור.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּמַאי קָמִיפַּלְגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After laying out both views on 'לך יהיה' and 'בשרם', the גמרא now looks for the root principle behind their argument.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What principle actually divides רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא?

steps.title: A law from a היקש plus another source: is it a היקש?
steps.stepSummary: One view holds that a law coming from a היקש and also from another source counts as a היקש. The other view holds it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: One master holds: something learned from it [the היקש] together with something else is considered a היקש. The other master holds: it is not considered a היקש.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question. The argument is about a law that comes partly from a היקש and partly from somewhere else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ישמעאל says this mixed case still counts as a היקש, so the תודה cannot pass its law on to the בכור. רבי עקיבא says it does not count as a היקש, so the תודה can still teach through a היקש.

keyTerms.meaning: One master holds
From it and from something else: a law with two sources
It counts as a היקש

steps.confusionAlert: They do not argue about the basic rule that a היקש cannot teach through another היקש. They both accept that rule. They only argue about the mixed case, where the law also has another source.

phrases.english: One master holds: from it and from something else —
phrases.notes: He means a law that comes partly from the היקש and partly from another source.

phrases.english: is a היקש;
and the other master holds: it is not a היקש.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָר סָבַר הֵימֶנּוּ וְדָבָר אַחֵר הָוֵי הֶיקֵּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 23.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The argument is whether a law coming from a היקש and from another source is treated as a היקש (רבי ישמעאל) or not (רבי עקיבא).
steps.whyThisMatters: This turns a specific argument about the תודה and the בכור into a general rule about how היקש works. The rest of the discussion builds on it.

steps.title: The view 'not a היקש' fits the יום כפור פסוק
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the view that a mixed case is not a היקש explains the פסוק 'וכן יעשה לאהל מועד'.
steps.simpleTranslation: It works well for the one who says it is not a היקש. That is why it is written: 'And so shall he do for the Tent of Meeting.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts to show that one view fits a פסוק about יום כפור. The word בשלמא ('it works well for...') tells us a challenge against the other view is coming.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא brings the פסוק about the כהן גדול's sprinklings as support for the view that a mixed case is not a היקש. The next step spells out how the פסוק works.

keyTerms.meaning: It works well for... (usually followed by a problem for the other side)
That is why it is written
The Tent of Meeting; here, the outer room of the Sanctuary

phrases.english: It works well for the one who says
it is not a היקש,
that is why it is written:
"And so shall he do for the Tent of Meeting" —
phrases.notes: ויקרא 16:16, about the כהן גדול's service on יום כפור.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר לָא הָוֵי הֶיקֵּשׁ הַיְינוּ דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the two views from step 24 against a פסוק.
steps.raayaObject: The view that a law from a היקש plus another source is not a היקש.

steps.title: How the sprinklings are copied from inside to the היכל
steps.stepSummary: Just as the כהן גדול sprinkles once up and seven times down inside the קודש הקדשים with the bull's blood and the goat's blood, he does the same in the היכל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Just as he sprinkles in the innermost room once upward and seven times downward from the bull's blood, so he sprinkles in the היכל. And just as in the innermost room it is once upward and seven times downward from the goat's blood, so he sprinkles in the היכל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what the פסוק 'וכן יעשה' teaches. The pattern of sprinkling in the innermost room is copied to the היכל, for both the bull and the goat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The details of the goat's sprinkling inside are themselves learned from the bull. Then the היכל sprinkling is learned from that, so something learned is teaching again. This works for the view that such a mixed case is not a היקש, and it sets up a problem for the other view.

keyTerms.meaning: The innermost room, the קודש הקדשים
The outer room of the Sanctuary
Once upward and seven times downward: the יום כפור sprinkling pattern
The bull and the goat of יום כפור

steps.whatToRemember: The two views split over a law that comes from a היקש plus another source. The יום כפור sprinklings, copied from inside to the היכל for both bull and goat, fit the view that such a case is not a היקש.

phrases.english: Just as he sprinkles in the innermost room
once upward and seven times downward
from the blood of the bull,
so he sprinkles in the היכל.
And just as in the innermost room
it is once upward and seven times downward
from the blood of the goat,
so he sprinkles in the היכל.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּשֵׁם שֶׁמַּזֶּה לִפְנַי וְלִפְנִים אַחַת לְמַעְלָה וְשֶׁבַע לְמַטָּה מִדַּם הַפָּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the meaning of the פסוק brought in step 25.
steps.raayaObject: A law learned from a היקש plus another source can still teach further, so it is not treated as a היקש.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The sprinklings of the bull and the goat, copied from the innermost room to the היכל through 'וכן יעשה לאהל מועד'.

steps.title: The challenge to the view that a mixed case counts as a היקש
steps.stepSummary: According to the view that a mixed case counts as a היקש, how can the היכל sprinkling be learned from the קודש הקדשים sprinkling?
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to the one who says it is considered a היקש, what can be said?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the second view and asks how that view can explain the פסוק 'וכן יעשה לאהל מועד'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rules about the blood inside the קודש הקדשים were themselves learned through a היקש. If a mixed case counts as a היקש, then copying those rules over to the היכל means a היקש is teaching another היקש. In קדשים that is not allowed, so this view seems to be stuck.

keyTerms.meaning: According to the one who says
It counts as a היקש (a comparison the תורה makes by placing two things together)
What can be said? (This view seems to have a problem.)

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not about the first view at all. Step 25 already said the first view has no problem. This question is only aimed at the view that a mixed case does count as a היקש.

phrases.english: But according to the one who says it is a היקש,
phrases.notes: This is the view from Step 24 that a law coming from a היקש plus another source still counts as a היקש.

phrases.english: what can be said?
phrases.notes: He means: how can the היכל learn from the קודש הקדשים, if that would be a היקש learning from a היקש?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר הָוֵי הֶיקֵּשׁ, מַאי אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After showing that the first view explains the פסוק easily, the גמרא challenges the second view on the same פסוק.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that a law from a היקש mixed with another source counts as a היקש
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under this view, learning the היכל sprinkling from the קודש הקדשים sprinkling would be a היקש teaching another היקש, which is not allowed in קדשים.

steps.title: The places are compared, not the bloods
steps.stepSummary: The second comparison is between the locations of sprinkling, so it is not a היקש built on another היקש.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is the places that are learned from one another.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The פסוק compares the place called the היכל to the place called the קודש הקדשים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first היקש compared the bull's blood to the goat's blood. The second comparison does not deal with the bloods at all. It compares the sprinkling in one place to the sprinkling in another place. The places themselves were never learned through a היקש, so nothing learned by a היקש is being used to teach again.

keyTerms.meaning: Places: here, the קודש הקדשים and the היכל where the blood is sprinkled
They learn (are derived)
From one another

steps.whatToRemember: Even under the view that a mixed case counts as a היקש, 'וכן יעשה לאהל מועד' works. The first comparison is blood to blood, and the second is place to place. These are two separate comparisons, not one היקש stacked on another.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that both views of רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא can explain the פסוק. So this פסוק does not decide between them.

phrases.english: It is the places that are learned from one another.

steps.triggerLanguage: מְקוֹמוֹת הוּא דְּגָמְרִי מֵהֲדָדֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 27.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought the היכל was learning the blood rules that were themselves learned by a היקש. That would be a היקש from a היקש.
steps.terutzMaskana: The second comparison is place to place, so it does not build on the first היקש.
